slides.h: Anyone can change the name on your certificate
Try it on the last one you sent
slides.b:
· Open the PDF in any free editor
· Type a different name
· Save it, it looks identical

slides.h: Nothing on the file can be checked
slides.b:
· A logo anyone can copy
· A signature that is an image
· No way to ask you if it is real

slides.h: What a real check looks like
slides.b:
· One link per certificate
· It names the issuer and the date
· It fails loudly if the file was touched

slides.h: Schools already issue them this way
slides.b: Diplomy (diplomy.org) gives every certificate its own verification page, under your school's brand.

slides.h: The name on it should not be editable

slides.h: Do this before you send your next batch of certificates

slides.b:
· What the student actually had to do
· Hours, project, exam, attendance
· One line, printed on the certificate

· Safety and compliance renew yearly
· A finished course does not expire
· Either way, print the issue date

slides.h: Keep a way to pull one back
slides.b:
· Wrong name, wrong course, wrong person
· It happens in every batch
· An emailed file can never be pulled back

slides.h: We issue ours the same way
slides.b: Diplomy (diplomy.org) carries the criteria, the expiry and the revocation on every certificate you send.

slides.h: Ten minutes before the batch, not after
